rationale: Hebrew yod/waw/heth/nun/nun is proposed by script correspondence. Greek Giochanan is a readability-oriented spelling, not a reversible mapping or a claim about first-century sound, stress, gemination or East/West Syriac vowels. Greek chi does not exactly represent Syriac heth; no equivalent sound is claimed. Conventional localized Ioannis is not silently substituted. Full source form retained in source text and registry.
support: Noldeke/Crichton 1904, Compendious Syriac Grammar §§1–4, especially letter table and approximate pronunciation/vowel-letter distinctions; target name spelling is editorial, not attested there.
uncertainty: The unpointed source does not authorize a unique vocalization. Readers must not treat Greek spelling as pronunciation evidence. No audio or reconstructed original is provided.
